$comment: Machine-readable current-state attestation for Russell Vault, owned by this repository.
It is a BOUNDED PROJECTION of verified truth, not a live mirror of production.
Every claim below carries an explicit evidenceClass. Read evidenceClasses first.
Validated by scripts/ci/current-state-guard.mjs (unit tests in current-state-guard.test.mjs).
It is deliberately NOT pinned to exact HEAD: only a change to the governed migration
set forces an update, so documentation-only commits never invalidate it.

evidenceClasses.deployed_config: Read directly from the deployed Railway service configuration or the deployed application bundle. The only class that may establish production identity.
evidenceClasses.live_schema: Read directly from a live Supabase database over an authenticated connection. Proves what a database contains, never which database production uses.
evidenceClasses.repository: Read from files at the reviewed commit in this repository.
evidenceClasses.github_api: Read from the GitHub API for an exact SHA, run id, and run attempt.
evidenceClasses.unmerged: Present only on an open pull request. Never an executable baseline.
evidenceClasses.not_inspectable: Could not be inspected from the verifying environment. Recorded as a blocker, never silently downgraded into a claim about reality.

$comment: expectedCount and lastMigrationName describe the REPOSITORY migration set at the
reviewed SHA. setDigest is sha256 over the sorted migration basenames without the
'.sql' suffix, one per line, each line newline-terminated. The digest catches a
replaced or renamed migration that leaves the count unchanged.
Production identity is ESTABLISHED, on the authority of the repository owner's declaration.
It was NOT read from the deployed Railway runtime — see independentRuntimeInspection, which
must keep saying so. A ledger or fingerprint that matches the repository is corroboration
about what a database CONTAINS; it is never evidence of which database the deployed service
is configured to use, and it is recorded here as corroboration only.
An established identity is not a licence to deploy: see preDeploymentRequirement.
deploymentIdentity.authoritativeSource: Declaration by the repository owner (kam032289@gmail.com) in the 'Production Identity and Supabase Preview Integrity' follow-up work order
deploymentIdentity.independentRuntimeInspection: NOT PERFORMED. No verifying environment has reached the deployed Railway service or the live app host: the egress policy answered 403 to CONNECT for russellvault2-production.up.railway.app:443, and Railway environment variables are not stored in this repository. Nothing in this file may be read as a claim that the deployed runtime was inspected.
deploymentIdentity.corroboration: Read-only catalog inspection of ncyqqitqtsyjrijieykd on 2026-08-26 agrees with the declaration: governed public.schema_migrations_log at 79 with this repository's tail, 119 public tables whose sha256 over sorted names is identical to the local 80-migration replay, 54 enums, 17 views, all four governed marker tables, 8 receiving RPCs, migration 80 not applied, and the three ESC-002 receiving functions still carrying unnamed parameters. Corroboration agrees with the declaration; it does not substitute for it, and neither substitutes for resolving the live target before acting.
deploymentIdentity.preDeploymentRequirement: Every migration, deployment, reset, restore or parity claim must still resolve the Supabase target from the environment it is about to act on, immediately before acting, and confirm it equals canonicalProjectRef. scripts/ci/production-target-guard.mjs performs exactly that comparison and fails closed. A declaration fixes the expected answer; it does not confirm that the environment in front of you matches it.
deploymentIdentity.destructiveActionRule: No live action may rely on this file for production identity. Before any live Supabase read, migration, reset, restore, or parity claim, re-read the deployed Supabase URL from the running environment immediately before acting, and confirm the target project ref matches it. A remembered ref, a project display name, a scoped project listing, an agent handoff, and this attestation are all insufficient.
$stateMachine: verificationPerformed is the SINGLE state variable for 'is there an established identity'.
evidenceClass says on what AUTHORITY. There is deliberately no second boolean: a duplicate flag
could be left saying one thing while every other field says the other. The guard rejects a
UNVERIFIED (verificationPerformed=false) requires: canonicalProjectRef=null; zero registry entries
with a production role; evidenceClass=not_inspectable; a nonempty blocker; verifiedAtUtc=null;
verificationMethod=null; and no canonical document asserting any production project.
registry entry with role owner_declared_production and evidenceClass owner_declaration, equal to
canonicalProjectRef; blocker cleared; verifiedAtUtc, verificationMethod and authoritativeSource
populated; and independentRuntimeInspection, corroboration and preDeploymentRequirement all nonempty.
RUNTIME_VERIFIED (verificationPerformed=true, evidenceClass=deployed_config) requires the same shape
with role deployed_production and evidenceClass deployed_config on both halves.
OWNER_DECLARED is a real, weaker-evidence state, not a lesser version of RUNTIME_VERIFIED: the owner
settles WHICH project is canonical, and the deployment guard still has to resolve the live target
and match it before anything is applied.
Every transition is all-or-nothing: a partial edit fails CI rather than half-asserting an identity.
deploymentIdentity.verificationMethod: Repository-owner declaration in the 'Production Identity and Supabase Preview Integrity' follow-up work order, recorded together with read-only catalog corroboration. The deployed Railway runtime was NOT read; see independentRuntimeInspection.

$comment: Every Supabase project ref that appears in a canonical document must be registered here.
role 'deployed_production' may only be assigned when deploymentIdentity.verificationPerformed
is true. The guard enforces both rules.
